- Flatten enables the recursive conversion of an array-like variable into a flat slice of `[]interface{}`. For example, invoking `Flatten([]interface{"foo", []int{2, 3}})` yields `[]interface{}{"foo", 2, 3}`. This method is compatible with builder methods such as `In`, `NotIn`, `Values`, etc., facilitating the conversion of a typed array into `[]interface{}` or the merging of inputs.

- List operates similarly to `Flatten`, with the exception that its return value is specifically intended for use as builder arguments. For example, `Buildf("my_func(%v)", List([]int{1, 2, 3})).Build()` generates SQL `my_func(?, ?, ?)` with arguments `[]interface{}{1, 2, 3}`.
- Raw designates a string as a "raw string" within arguments. For instance, `Buildf("SELECT %v", Raw("NOW()")).Build()` results in SQL `SELECT NOW()`.

Gamma is a **membership and identity management system** built for Chalmers IT student division. It serves as the central directory for members, groups, OAuth2 clients, and API keys.

When `PRODUCTION=false` or `IS_MOCKING=true`, Gamma loads mock data from `MOCK_DATA_RESOURCE` (default `mock.json`) on startup. Each kind of data is only created if none of it exists yet. All mock users sign in with the password `password1337`.
|`clientId`|OAuth2 client ID, exactly 30 upper case letters and digits|
|`clientSecret`|Raw client secret, encoded when the client is created|
|`emailScope`|Whether the client gets the `email` scope in addition to `openid profile`|
|`ownerId`|Id of the user that owns the client. Leave it out for an official client|
|`apiKey`|Optional client API key. Use it with `Authorization: pre-shared <id>:<token>`|
|`authorities`|Authority names (2-30 lower case letters and digits) with the ids of the super groups and users that have them|

|`PRODUCTION`|`true`|Production mode (disables Thymeleaf caching, dev services, etc.)|
|`OAUTH2_SIGNING_KEY`|*(empty)*|RSA private key that signs OAuth2 tokens. Will be required in production from v3, see OAuth2 signing keys|
|`OAUTH2_VERIFICATION_KEYS`|*(empty)*|Comma separated keys that are still published so the tokens they signed can be verified, but that no longer sign tokens|

Gamma signs ID tokens and access tokens with the RSA key in `OAUTH2_SIGNING_KEY` and publishes its public key at `/oauth2/jwks`. Without one, a temporary key is generated on every start, so tokens stop working when Gamma restarts and instances can't verify each other's tokens. Running in production without `OAUTH2_SIGNING_KEY` is deprecated, and Gamma v3 will refuse to start without it (#1004).

Both settings take PEM content directly or the location of a PEM file, such as `/run/secrets/gamma-signing-key.pem` or `file:/run/secrets/gamma-signing-key.pem`. Each key gets its RFC 7638 thumbprint as key id (`kid`), so every instance that uses the same key publishes the same key id. Keys must be RSA keys of at least 2048 bits.

Under it, `persia-engine` creates and opens a database file, puts, deletes and commits documents through a WAL, merges segments, and runs a ranked search over a collection snapshot: user text compiled to a query, BM25F scoring, filters, sorts, facets, and pages. Relaxation (M8) is not built, so a search that matches nothing returns no hits. A small CLI inspects and verifies files.

**Space:** dead frames (replaced segments, old manifests, consumed WAL chunks) are reclaimed by compacting the container (SPEC §4.6). Call `Database::compact` to compact now; besides, every `merge_step` compacts when dead bytes reach 40% of the file and at least 1 MiB, unless `CompactionOptions::automatic` is turned off (`DatabaseOptions::compaction`). `Database::space_usage` reports the live and dead bytes.

The on-disk layout is a versioned format of this repository, specified in `SPEC.md` (draft v0.1). Anything written is little-endian and covered by a checksum. A layout change updates the SPEC, bumps a version or a feature flag, adds an ADR under `docs/adr/`, and adds a golden fixture. Segments are immutable once written.
|Container|`header.rs`, SPEC §4|Magic `PERSIA\0\x01`, format **1.0**, a 4096-byte header, two superblock slots, then frames. `format_major` 1 is the only major this build reads.|
|Segment|`segment/write.rs`, SPEC §5|Footer magic `PSEG`, format **1.0**. Sections, then the footer. `SegmentWriter` produces the bytes; `Segment::open` checks them.|
|CRC32C|`checksum.rs`|Castagnoli CRC on headers, frames, and blocks. A mismatch is `Error::Corrupt`, with the offset of the stored checksum.|
|zstd|`compress.rs`, ADR-0005|Block codec `Zstd` or `None`. Decode requires the uncompressed length the block header declared, and returns `Error::Corrupt` for any other length.|
|XXH3|`hash.rs`|XXH3-64 and XXH3-128, default secret, seed 0, for content and routing hashes. Integrity is CRC32C. Blob ids are SHA-256 (ADR-0002).|
|mmap|`mmap.rs`, ADR-0010|Read-only mapping of an immutable file range. A fault on a mapped page ends the process. Callers that cannot accept that use positioned reads.|
|`ByteSource`|`source.rs`|One buffer type for mapped, heap, and cached bytes. Clone and `slice` share the underlying `bytes::Bytes` (or the mapping) without copying the payload.|

|Unicode|`persia-analysis`, SPEC §6.3|UAX #29 word boundaries and NFKC, pinned to Unicode **17.0.0**. Built-in analyzers: `standard`, `keyword`, `whitespace`, `en`, `es`, `pt`, `fr`, `de`, `it`. Stemmers for German, English, Spanish, French, Italian, and Portuguese.|
|Fuzzing|`fuzz/fuzz_targets`, `.github/workflows/fuzz.yml`|cargo-fuzz on every target. Pull requests lint the fuzz crate. The scheduled workflow runs the targets on a dated nightly.|

|CI|`.github/workflows/ci.yml`|`rustfmt`, clippy `-D warnings` on the workspace and the fuzz crate, `cargo test --workspace` on Linux and macOS, format and storage tests on Windows, Miri on `persia-format` and the pure parsers of `persia-engine`, `cargo deny` (bans, licenses, sources), dependency direction, golden fixtures, and a fresh `PROGRESS.md`. Advisories run daily.|

Rust is the native API. The facade crate is `persia`, a placeholder until M10. The libraries under it are what a Rust caller can use today, as in the quickstart.

Go and TypeScript embedded bindings are planned for **v1.1** (M16). The design is ADR-0018 and `docs/sdk/`, and it is not implemented. One C ABI (`persia-ffi`) wraps `persia`. Go calls it through cgo (`sdk/persia`). TypeScript calls it through N-API (`@persiadb/node`) for Node.js, Bun, and Deno. Ranking, relaxation, and crash recovery stay in the Rust core.

The engineering rules in `CLAUDE.md` bind those changes the same way they bind a human patch. `SPEC.md` is the contract. A byte string from disk, the network, or a user that fails a check comes back as `Err`. A change to the on-disk layout updates the SPEC, bumps a version or a feature flag, adds an ADR, and adds a golden fixture.
